name: New Coke
tierWhy: Coca-Cola took the 1985 formula off the market in the early 2000s, but in 2019 it partnered with Netflix “to temporarily bring back 1985’s New Coke” in a limited run of cans for “Stranger Things”; we found nothing sold under the name since.[^21][^25][^31]

title: New Coke (1985–2002): post-mortem · Spectre Brands
description: Coca-Cola changed its formula on April 23, 1985 and brought the old one back 79 days later. New Coke and Coke II, followed from the wire reports of 1985 and Coca-Cola’s own account to the 2019 re-release.

card.blurb: Nearly 200,000 taste tests said the new formula was better. Coca-Cola replaced the old one with it, took 1,500 calls a day, and reversed itself in 79 days. The new drink stayed on sale for years as Coke II.

stat.label: from the new formula’s launch to the return of the old one

hero.dates: Announced April 23, 1985. Old formula restored July 1985. Renamed Coke II from 1990. Withdrawn in the early 2000s.
hero.standfirst: The taste tests said people preferred it. Nobody had asked them how they would feel if the old one was taken away.
hero.deck: On April 23, 1985 the Coca-Cola Company replaced the formula of its flagship drink with a sweeter one that had won blind tests of nearly 200,000 people. Within weeks its hotline was taking 1,500 calls a day. On July 10 the company said the old formula would come back as Coca-Cola Classic, and the new one became the smaller of two Cokes, then Coke II, then nothing. The account rests on the wire reports of 1985, the company’s own published account and later reporting.
hero.artCaption: Original illustration of a red can with a silver wave. Not an official asset and not the trademarked design.

findings.title: The research was large, and it was about taste.
findings.text: A spokesman said more than 190,000 people preferred the new formula 55–45 blind and 61–39 when told what it was.[^4] Coca-Cola now says the tests did not show “the bond consumers felt with their Coca-Cola.”[^1]

findings.title: It did not join the old Coke. It replaced it.
findings.text: Production of the original stopped in April 1985.[^7] The complaint that followed was about the loss as much as the flavor.

findings.title: Trial was high and so was the noise.
findings.text: By June the company said 110 million people had tried it and about 80% would buy it again, while taking 1,500 mostly negative calls a day.[^5]

findings.title: The reversal took 79 days.
findings.text: The return of the old formula as Coca-Cola Classic was announced on July 10, 1985; Coca-Cola stock rose $2.37 that day.[^6][^8]

findings.title: The new formula outlived its failure by years.
findings.text: It stayed on sale as “Coke,” was tested as Coke II in Spokane in 1990, and was withdrawn in 2002 or 2004, depending on the source.[^13][^19][^21]
